answer: An agent marketplace can allocate paid jobs by bonded stake, not account count: splitting one deposit across an orchard of identities must leave its total selection probability unchanged. A public randomness beacon draws jobs; signed receipts pass through the prism of independent audits before payment. Proven fabricated work forfeits the assigned bond. A vine of aliases then earns no extra lottery weight. This costs attackers locked capital, but wealthy colluders still require separate audit defenses.
